Explanation
Explain the main signal, the context that matters, and what to check next.
How the overview works
What is combined
13 baseline scores form 12 domains: Iron Handling and Blood Flow Context share one domain. An overview needs at least 3 domains and 25% core coverage. Available domain results remain visible below that threshold. Excluded domains remain reflected in coverage; open Overview contributors to see exactly which scores are included.
What the colors mean
Green: strong range fit (70–100). Amber: review pattern (50–69). Red: lower range fit (0–49). These describe range agreement, not clinical severity.
Coverage stays separate
Missing core inputs reduce coverage. Additional tests add context without increasing a domain’s vote. Five optional scores stay outside the baseline.
Dates stay visible
Current domains use the collection-date limits. Historical and mixed-date estimates are labeled separately.

Explanation
Explain the main signal, the context that matters, and what to check next.
How the overview works
What is combined
13 baseline scores form 12 domains: Iron Handling and Blood Flow Context share one domain. An overview needs at least 3 domains and 25% core coverage. Available domain results remain visible below that threshold. Excluded domains remain reflected in coverage; open Overview contributors to see exactly which scores are included.
What the colors mean
Green: strong range fit (70–100). Amber: review pattern (50–69). Red: lower range fit (0–49). These describe range agreement, not clinical severity.
Coverage stays separate
Missing core inputs reduce coverage. Additional tests add context without increasing a domain’s vote. Five optional scores stay outside the baseline.
Dates stay visible
Current domains use the collection-date limits. Historical and mixed-date estimates are labeled separately.

What do kidney filtration and electrolyte results show, and could muscle mass affect them?

13 baseline scores form 12 domains: Iron Handling and Blood Flow Context share one domain. An overview needs at least 3 domains and 25% core coverage. Available domain results remain visible below that threshold. Excluded domains remain reflected in coverage; open Overview contributors to see exactly which scores are included.
What the colors mean
Green: strong range fit (70–100). Amber: review pattern (50–69). Red: lower range fit (0–49). These describe range agreement, not clinical severity.
Coverage stays separate
Missing core inputs reduce coverage. Additional tests add context without increasing a domain’s vote. Five optional scores stay outside the baseline.
Dates stay visible
Current domains use the collection-date limits. Historical and mixed-date estimates are labeled separately.
Interpretation notes 17
  • Built from minimum-panel Biology Score domains; extended-only scores improve depth but do not punish the baseline.
  • 0/12 minimum domains live.
  • 5 extended-only scores are outside the baseline coherence denominator.
  • Metabolic Flexibility: Needs fasting glucose and insulin, or HOMA-IR with usable collection and profile context before scoring.
  • Thyroid Coherence: Needs TSH and Free T4 with usable collection and profile context before scoring.
  • Cardiovascular Risk: Needs ApoB with usable collection and profile context before scoring.
  • Inflammatory Load: Needs CRP or hs-CRP with usable collection and profile context before scoring.
  • Blood Flow Context: Needs hemoglobin or hematocrit, plus platelets with usable collection and profile context before scoring.
  • Iron Handling: Needs ferritin plus transferrin saturation or hemoglobin with usable collection and profile context before scoring.
  • Methylation: Needs homocysteine plus B12 or folate with usable collection and profile context before scoring.
  • Kidney & Filtration: Needs an interpretable eGFR with usable collection and profile context before scoring.
  • Liver & Bile Flow: Needs ALT or AST, plus GGT or ALP with usable collection and profile context before scoring.
  • Bone & Mineral Balance: Needs calcium plus vitamin D or phosphorus with usable collection and profile context before scoring.
  • Immune Cell Balance: Needs WBC plus neutrophil or lymphocyte counts with usable collection and profile context before scoring.
  • Recovery Context: Needs profile-appropriate sex hormones plus albumin or total protein with usable collection and profile context before scoring.
  • Hormone Axis: Needs profile-appropriate sex hormones plus LH or FSH with usable collection and profile context before scoring.
  • An overview needs at least 3 domains and 25% core coverage. Your available domain results are shown below.

How this score works

What do kidney filtration and electrolyte results show, and could muscle mass affect them?

Filtration requires an interpretable eGFR and receives 70% of the complete core weight; sodium and potassium receive 15% each. Low muscle mass can make creatinine-based estimates misleading; cystatin-C eGFR offers another route. UACR adds kidney-damage context. Electrolytes alone cannot establish filtration or hydration.

How the overview works
What is combined
13 baseline scores form 12 domains: Iron Handling and Blood Flow Context share one domain. An overview needs at least 3 domains and 25% core coverage. Available domain results remain visible below that threshold. Excluded domains remain reflected in coverage; open Overview contributors to see exactly which scores are included.
What the colors mean
Green: strong range fit (70–100). Amber: review pattern (50–69). Red: lower range fit (0–49). These describe range agreement, not clinical severity.
Coverage stays separate
Missing core inputs reduce coverage. Additional tests add context without increasing a domain’s vote. Five optional scores stay outside the baseline.
Dates stay visible
Current domains use the collection-date limits. Historical and mixed-date estimates are labeled separately.

How this score works

How do TSH, Free T4 and Free T3 fit together, and what context could explain disagreement?

TSH and FT4 form the equally weighted core; FT3 adds active-hormone context. A same-draw FT3/FT4 ratio is descriptive, not a validated conversion-efficiency target. Medication timing, illness and biotin can change the pattern.

Core score
Weighted range fit of available core markers. Related measurements share a capped family weight. Missing core markers make the result provisional.
Additional markers
Support the core pattern, differ from it, or add a separate dimension. More tests do not automatically mean more confidence.
Range fit
Within the selected range = 100. Departure reduces fit linearly to a minimum of 0. The number describes range agreement, not a health probability.
Collection window
Current scores use results from the last 180 days, with core draws within 90 days of each other. Older and mixed-date estimates keep their date labels.

styleBlocks.css: .biology-score-unavailable-group > summary::before { content: '+'; margin-right: 8px; color: var(--text-muted); font-family: var(--font-mono); font-weight: 900; }

.biology-section-count { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; min-width: 24px; padding: 2px 6px; border-radius: 6px; background: var(--bg-secondary); border: 1px solid var(--border); font-size: 12px; color: var(--text-secondary); font-weight: 500; }
.biology-planning-grid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(2, minmax(0, 1fr)); gap: 16px; margin: 20px 0; align-items: stretch; }
.biology-score-group > h3, .biology-score-group > summary { margin: 0; font-size: 18px; color: var(--text-primary); font-weight: 650; }
.biology-score-group > p { margin: 8px 0 16px; font-size: 13px; line-height: 1.6; color: var(--text-secondary); max-width: 85ch; }
